reforms.description: The Canadian Government established Centres for Excellence linking top researchers from universities and major corporations, and initiated measures to support the creation of new sectoral or technological alliances involving government, the private sector, and the academic community. Both initiatives aimed to improve the efficiency of government R&D expenditure and address duplication and inadequate linkages between government laboratories, universities, and the private sector.
reforms.package_name: Government R&D Efficiency and Collaboration Initiative
reforms.component_name: Centres for Excellence and Sectoral Alliances
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Improved linkages between government, universities, and private sector reduce duplication and enhance R&D efficiency, supporting innovation and productivity gains.
reforms.status_evidence: Both descriptions indicate implemented status; inferred year is 1992 based on Economic Survey publication date.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant structural reform addressing systemic coordination failures in the R&D system, but narrower in scope than a complete system overhaul.
reforms.source_quote: The Government has initiated a number of programmes to address these problems. Among these is the establishment of the Centres for Excellence, which link up top researchers of universities and major corporations.

reforms.description: The Canadian Government proposed a policy reform to shift a greater proportion of government-funded research to the private sector, increase specialisation amongst universities, and complete the automation of the patent search process to improve the efficiency of government R&D expenditure.
reforms.package_name: Government R&D Efficiency and Collaboration Initiative
reforms.component_name: R&D Reallocation and Patent System Modernisation
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Shifting R&D to the private sector and automating patent search may enhance efficiency and commercialisation, but reducing government research capacity could hinder basic research and long-term innovation if not carefully managed.
reforms.status_evidence: Explicitly marked as announced in source data.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant reallocation of R&D funding and governance, but announced rather than implemented, and narrower than a complete system restructuring.
reforms.source_quote: Efficiency could, however, be further improved by shifting a greater proportion of government-funded research to the private sector, increasing specialisation amongst universities and rapidly completing the automation of the patent search process.

reforms.description: The Canadian Government proposed increased emphasis on technology diffusion programmes in its R&D policy, recognising that the ability to create technology is outstripping the ability to use it, and that diffusing existing technologies is a relatively low-cost way to enhance technological capability, particularly beneficial for small firms.
reforms.package_name: Government R&D Efficiency and Collaboration Initiative
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Technology diffusion programmes enhance the utilisation of existing innovations, particularly benefiting small firms, and represent a cost-effective approach to raising technological capability and productivity.
reforms.status_evidence: Explicitly marked as announced in source data.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant policy reorientation towards diffusion and adoption, but announced rather than implemented, and narrower in scope than a complete system restructuring.
reforms.source_quote: One way in which this could be done is to focus more resources on the diffusion of technology. OECD nations are increasingly of the view that the ability to create technology is outstripping the ability to use it, and that diffusing existing technologies is a relatively low cost way to enhance technological capability.
